name: Solo
description: German Solo (often just called Solo) is a trick-taking game for 4 to 6 players, descended from l'Hombre. It is played with a 32-card pack (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit). Players bid for the right to choose trump and to play alone or with a called partner. The highest trump is always the Queen of Clubs, second is the 7 of trump, third is the Queen of Spades. The game survives in parts of the USA though little played in Germany today.
deck: 32 cards (French suits; A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 per suit)

history.origins: German Solo originated in Germany as a simplified version of l'Hombre (Ombre). American sources sometimes call it Modern Ombre. The fixed top trumps (Queen of Clubs, 7 of trump, Queen of Spades) show the Hombre lineage. In the late 18th century a three-hand variant was known as German Ombre (Dütsch Lumber) in northern Germany. The game is little played in Germany today but still played in parts of the USA.
timeline: 19th–20th century: German simplification of l'Hombre; six-bid auction and fixed top trumps (Club Q, 7 of trump, Spade Q).

setup.players: Four players (standard); five or six with dealer sitting out or buying a hand.
setup.deck: 32 cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit. For six players the 8 of hearts and 8 of diamonds are removed; 30 cards remain, 5 per player.
setup.dealing: Deal 8 cards each (4 players). A 3-2-3 or similar pattern; dealing starts to dealer's left. Dealer must verify each player has 8 cards before turning cards or a misdeal may be called. Deal rotates left after each hand.
setup.equipment: Standard playing cards; optionally chips or money for scoring.

rules.objective: As declarer (alone or with a called partner), make your contract: win the agreed number of tricks (e.g. 5 for Question/IsIt/Ladies/Solo, 6 for 6 Trick Solo, 8 for Bull Solo or Solo 2). As defenders, set the declarer by preventing the contract.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, bidding starts with the player to dealer's left. Each player may bid once (or pass). Bids in ascending order: Question, IsIt, Kicker, Having the Ladies, Solo, IsIt Solo, 6 Trick Solo, Bronco, Bull Solo, Solo 2. Highest bidder becomes declarer; in some bids the declarer calls an ace (not in hand) and its holder is partner. Trump is determined by the bid (e.g. Solo: declarer chooses; IsIt: clubs). Play: player to dealer's left leads; must follow suit when possible; trick won by highest card of led suit or highest trump. Trick winner leads next.
keyRules: Top three trumps are fixed: Queen of Clubs (highest), 7 of trump (second), Queen of Spades (third).
Bidder or partners must make the contracted number of tricks to score; otherwise defenders score.
In Kicker and Bronco the declarer must take zero tricks.

scoring.description: Score by bid value (e.g. Nickel Solo: bid value times 5 cents per opponent). Declarer pays each opponent if set; opponents pay declarer if contract is made. Mackers and First/Last add bonuses.
scoring.winCondition: Declarer (and partner if applicable) must win the contracted number of tricks (e.g. 5 for Question/IsIt/Solo, 6 for 6 Trick Solo, 8 for Bull Solo). If successful, declarer scores; otherwise defenders score.

synthesis.shortDescription: German Solo is a trick-taking game for 4 to 6 players with a 32-card pack. Players bid (Question, IsIt, Solo, etc.); top trumps are Club Q, 7 of trump, Spade Q.
